nodes.label: The Defence Ecosystem
nodes.does: The whole system, from strategy to the front line.

nodes.label: Strategy & Policy
nodes.does: Sets direction, budget and the demand signal.

nodes.label: Secretary of State for Defence
nodes.does: Political head of the MOD; owns SDR 2025 and the direction the whole system follows.

nodes.does: Re-aligned the MOD into Department of State, Military Strategic HQ, the NAD Group and the Defence Nuclear Enterprise.

nodes.label: Strategic Defence Review 2025
nodes.does: The root strategy — sets the threat picture, force design and the push for novel tech and faster procurement.

nodes.label: Defence Industrial Strategy 2025
nodes.does: ‘Making defence an engine for growth’ — industrial, SME, exports, skills and clusters agenda.

nodes.label: Military Strategic HQ
nodes.does: CDS-led; owns military strategy and the capability requirement that pulls innovation through.

nodes.label: Development, Concepts & Doctrine Centre (DCDC)

nodes.label: MOD Head Office

nodes.oppsOverride: MOD requirements advertised on the Defence Sourcing Portal and Find a Tender (www.find-tender.service.gov.uk).

nodes.label: Single Source Regulations Office (SSRO)
nodes.does: Regulates non-competitive contracts >£5m; sets the Baseline Profit Rate (9.10% for 2026/27).

nodes.label: Crown Commercial Service (CCS)
nodes.does: Cross-government commercial agreements used for common goods and services, incl. defence.

nodes.label: Science, Technology & Innovation
nodes.does: Where new capability is found, funded and de-risked.

nodes.label: Dstl

nodes.oppsOverride: Research opportunities via the Serapis framework and R-Cloud; tenders on Contracts Finder (www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk).

nodes.label: UK Defence Innovation (UKDI)
nodes.entry: Single front door · GOV.UK submission service
nodes.does: Consolidated innovation body (£400m/yr; £1.6bn in the DIP); runs Open Call, Themed and Loan competitions.
nodes.oppsOverride: UKDI competitions — including the multi-cycle ‘Innovation Support to Operations’ themed competition (fast, TRL 6+, months not years) plus wider themed and loan routes. Live cycles and the five innovation themes appear on gov.uk and the UKDI submission service.
nodes.funding: Funds directly. The UK Defence Innovation front door channels problem-holders to funded competitions and pipelines; award sizes vary by route.

nodes.label: Defence & Security Accelerator (DASA)
nodes.entry: GOV.UK › DASA · accelerator@dstl.gov.uk · online submission service
nodes.does: Finds and funds exploitable innovation fast; the established SME competition route. Became part of UKDI in February 2026 and continues to run its competitions.
nodes.oppsOverride: DASA finds and funds exploitable innovation through themed and open competitions; now part of UKDI and running its cycles. Current competitions are listed on gov.uk (search ‘DASA’ or ‘UKDI competitions’). Contact accelerator@dstl.gov.uk.
nodes.funding: Funds directly. Runs themed and open competitions; typical DASA contracts run from tens of thousands up to a few million pounds per project, paid as R&D contracts (not grants or equity).

nodes.does: Former standalone innovation unit, now consolidated into UKDI; brokered defence problems to commercial solutions.

nodes.label: UI (Sweden)

nodes.label: Think Tank EUROPA (Denmark)

nodes.label: PISM (Poland)

nodes.label: Casimir Pulaski Foundation (Poland)
nodes.does: Independent Warsaw think tank focused on defence, security and transatlantic relations; runs Defence24-adjacent expert networks.

nodes.label: GLOBSEC (Slovakia)
nodes.does: Bratislava-headquartered global think tank; its European Defence Initiative and Eastern-flank readiness reports are widely cited.

nodes.label: SFPA (Slovakia)

nodes.label: IIR Prague (Czechia)

nodes.label: AMO (Czechia)
nodes.does: Association for International Affairs — independent Prague think tank on foreign and security policy.

nodes.label: PSSI (Czechia)
nodes.does: Prague Security Studies Institute — security policy, economic security and space-security programmes.

nodes.label: New Strategy Center (Romania)
nodes.does: Romanian think tank on Black Sea security, defence and energy.

nodes.label: Sofia Security Forum (Bulgaria)
nodes.does: Bulgarian platform convening South-East European security and defence debate.

nodes.label: BCSP (Serbia)
nodes.does: Belgrade Centre for Security Policy — security-sector research in the Western Balkans.

nodes.label: DCAF (Geneva)
nodes.does: Geneva Centre for Security Sector Governance — a global reference on democratic governance of armed and security forces.

nodes.label: IRIS (France)
nodes.does: Institut de relations internationales et stratégiques — French institute with a strong defence-economics and strategy focus.

nodes.label: FRS (France)
nodes.does: Fondation pour la Recherche Stratégique — the leading independent French think tank working exclusively on defence and international security (deterrence, proliferation, strategy).

nodes.label: IRSEM (France)
nodes.does: Institut de Recherche Stratégique de l'École Militaire — the Ministry of the Armed Forces' strategic research institute (attached to DGRIS); studies on defence policy and strategy.

nodes.label: SWP (Germany)
nodes.does: Stiftung Wissenschaft und Politik — the German government's principal foreign & security policy advisory institute, Berlin.

nodes.label: DGAP (Germany)
nodes.does: German Council on Foreign Relations — a leading independent think tank on foreign, security and defence policy, Berlin.

nodes.label: IAI (Italy)
nodes.does: Istituto Affari Internazionali — Italy's leading defence and international-affairs institute, Rome.

nodes.label: ISPI (Italy)
nodes.does: Institute for International Political Studies — Milan-based foreign-policy and security think tank.

nodes.label: Elcano Royal Institute (Spain)
nodes.does: Spain's leading international and strategic studies institute, Madrid.

nodes.label: CIDOB (Spain)
nodes.does: Barcelona Centre for International Affairs — foreign and security policy research.

nodes.label: Clingendael (Netherlands)
nodes.does: The Netherlands Institute of International Relations — leading think tank and diplomatic academy, part-funded by the Dutch MoD.

nodes.label: HCSS (Netherlands)
nodes.does: The Hague Centre for Strategic Studies — data-driven security, defence-industrial and strategic analysis.

nodes.label: NUPI (Norway)
nodes.does: Norwegian Institute of International Affairs — Oslo; security, defence and Arctic research.

nodes.label: PRIO (Norway)
nodes.does: Peace Research Institute Oslo — long-standing conflict and security research institute.

nodes.label: DIIS (Denmark)
nodes.does: Danish Institute for International Studies — foreign, defence and security policy research, Copenhagen.

nodes.label: ELIAMEP (Greece)
nodes.does: Hellenic Foundation for European & Foreign Policy — Greece's principal international-affairs think tank.

nodes.label: IPRI-NOVA (Portugal)
nodes.does: Portuguese Institute of International Relations — NOVA University Lisbon; foreign and security policy.

nodes.label: KKI / IFAT (Hungary)
nodes.does: Institute for Foreign Affairs and Trade — Hungary's government-linked international-affairs institute.

nodes.label: CGAI (Canada)
nodes.does: Canadian Global Affairs Institute — Canada's leading independent defence, security and foreign-policy institute (Calgary/Ottawa).

nodes.label: CDA Institute (Canada)
nodes.does: Conference of Defence Associations Institute — a long-standing non-partisan think tank on Canadian defence and security policy (Ottawa).

nodes.label: ASPI (Australia)
nodes.does: Australian Strategic Policy Institute — Canberra; defence and strategic policy, widely cited across the Indo-Pacific.

nodes.label: JIIA (Japan)
nodes.does: Japan Institute of International Affairs — Japan's leading foreign-policy and security think tank, Tokyo.

nodes.label: KIDA (South Korea)
nodes.does: Korea Institute for Defense Analyses — the ROK's principal government defence-analysis institute.

nodes.label: INSS (Israel)
nodes.does: Institute for National Security Studies — Israel's leading security think tank, Tel Aviv University.

nodes.label: JISS (Israel)
nodes.does: Jerusalem Institute for Strategy and Security — national-security research and strategy.

nodes.label: National Strategies & Policy Documents
nodes.does: The published strategies and reviews that set defence direction — the actual instruments, each linked to the official source that carries it. Documents are periodically replaced, so confirm you're reading the current edition.

nodes.label: UK Strategic Defence Review 2025
nodes.does: 'Making Britain Safer: secure at home, strong abroad' — the externally-led SDR published 2 June 2025; 62 recommendations, NATO-first, a shift to war-fighting readiness, autonomy and AI.

nodes.label: UK National Security Strategy 2025
nodes.does: The cross-government National Security Strategy published June 2025 ahead of the NATO Hague Summit; sets the UK's threat assessment and security priorities above the defence-specific SDR.

nodes.label: NATO Strategic Concept 2022
nodes.does: The Alliance's guiding document, approved at the Madrid Summit on 29 June 2022 — three core tasks (deterrence & defence; crisis prevention & management; cooperative security); names Russia the most significant and direct threat.

nodes.label: EU Strategic Compass 2022
nodes.does: The EU's security & defence action plan to 2030, adopted March 2022 — a shared threat analysis and concrete goals including the EU Rapid Deployment Capacity.

nodes.label: US National Defense Strategy
nodes.does: The Department of Defense's capstone strategy directing force posture, priorities and the pacing challenge; issued by the Secretary of Defense and published via defense.gov.

nodes.label: US National Security Strategy
nodes.does: The White House's overarching statement of national-security priorities, from which the National Defense Strategy flows.

nodes.label: France — Revue Nationale Stratégique
nodes.does: France's National Strategic Review (first issued 2022, Toulon) — sets ten strategic objectives; maintained by the SGDSN under the Prime Minister.

nodes.label: Germany — National Security Strategy
nodes.does: Germany's first integrated National Security Strategy (2023), the 'Zeitenwende' turning point — an 'integrated security' approach across defence, resilience and values.

nodes.label: EU Capability Development Priorities
nodes.does: The European Defence Agency's agreed capability priorities that steer collaborative EU development — the practical companion to the Strategic Compass.

nodes.label: Defence Banking & Finance
nodes.does: Debt, lending and public financial institutions willing to serve defence — distinct from equity investors. A fast-moving layer as Europe and NATO rebuild defence-positive finance.

nodes.label: Defence, Security & Resilience Bank (DSRB)
nodes.does: Proposed nation-owned multilateral bank to harness capital markets for allied defence, readiness and supply-chain finance; in development, backed by major banks and 30+ nations.

nodes.label: European Investment Bank — Security & Defence
nodes.does: The EU's bank; has expanded defence eligibility and intermediated lending to reach defence-supply-chain SMEs across the Union.

nodes.label: KfW (Germany)
nodes.does: Germany's national promotional bank; part of the EIB-coordinated pan-European defence-finance push.

nodes.label: Bpifrance
nodes.does: France's public investment bank — dedicated defence support, loans and equity for defence SMEs.

nodes.label: Cassa Depositi e Prestiti (Italy)
nodes.does: Italy's national promotional institution participating in the pan-European defence-finance framework.

nodes.label: Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego (Poland)
nodes.does: Poland's state development bank, financing the Eastern flank's rapid rearmament.

nodes.label: ICO (Spain)
nodes.does: Instituto de Crédito Oficial — Spain's national promotional bank in the EIB defence-finance group.

nodes.label: Caisse des Dépôts (France)
nodes.does: France's long-term public investor, part of the five-nation promotional-bank defence agreement.

nodes.label: Dual-Use Incubators & Accelerators
nodes.does: Programmes that take dual-use and defence-tech founders from idea to first contract — hands-on cohorts, mentoring and access, distinct from pure investors.

nodes.label: Starburst Aerospace
nodes.does: Global aerospace & defence accelerator connecting start-ups with primes, investors and governments.

nodes.label: NSIN (US)
nodes.does: National Security Innovation Network — US DoD programme building defence-tech talent and ventures via university and start-up communities.

nodes.label: Techstars (Defense/Space)
nodes.does: Global accelerator running defence- and space-focused programmes with government and prime partners.

nodes.label: Plexal
nodes.does: UK innovation company delivering defence and cyber accelerators (e.g. for DASA and NCSC), based at Here East.

nodes.label: D3 / Dual-use VC
nodes.does: Dual-use venture investor backing defence and deep-tech founders; runs accelerator-style community programmes.

nodes.label: Hacking for Defense (BMNT)
nodes.does: Problem-curation and H4D methodology connecting mission problems to start-up solutions; US-origin, now allied.

nodes.label: LORCA / Cyber Runway alumni
nodes.does: UK cyber and dual-use scale-up programmes feeding the defence supply chain.

nodes.label: Startupbootcamp (Def/Sec)
nodes.does: Global accelerator network running defence- and security-relevant cohorts in Europe.

nodes.label: Tehnopol (Estonia)
nodes.does: The Baltics' largest science & business park, Tallinn; runs Estonia's NATO DIANA accelerator and cyber/dual-use programmes.

nodes.label: Palladion Defence Accelerator (Germany)
nodes.does: Germany's DIANA defence accelerator, based at the University of the Bundeswehr Munich — deep-tech and dual-use maturation with Bundeswehr links.

nodes.label: European Defense Tech Hackathon (Eurodefense.tech)
nodes.does: Community running Europe's largest defence-tech hackathons (Munich, Tallinn and beyond) — the recurring collaborative events connecting builders to the sector.

nodes.label: DEFINE — Defence Innovation Network Finland
nodes.does: Finland's defence-innovation network; co-delivers the Finnish NATO DIANA accelerator with VTT, Aalto University and the University of Helsinki.

nodes.label: Defence Communications & Engagement
nodes.does: Specialist agencies that help defence and security organisations communicate, engage stakeholders and navigate the sector — a practical enabler for SMEs and primes alike.

nodes.label: Canny Comms
nodes.does: Defence & security communications and marketing consultancy (Porton Down Science Park); runs the CIPR-accredited Reputation Masterclass and training for the sector.

nodes.label: Black Jellyfish
nodes.does: Technology consultancy partnering on defence communications and complex-technology engagement.

nodes.label: Procurement Frameworks & Vehicles
nodes.does: The framework agreements and buying vehicles suppliers actually contract through — the plumbing beneath the tender portals.

nodes.label: Crown Commercial Service
nodes.does: The UK government's central buying function; hosts framework agreements many defence and public-sector requirements run through.

nodes.label: DE&S Commercial frameworks
nodes.does: Defence Equipment & Support lets and manages the major MOD framework agreements and enabling contracts.

nodes.label: DSPCR 2011
nodes.does: The Defence & Security Public Contracts Regulations — the framework that governed UK defence procurement. Note: the Procurement Act 2023 came into force 24 Feb 2025 and DSPCR guidance is no longer maintained for new procurements — see Cabinet Office PA 2023 guidance.

nodes.label: Defence Sourcing Portal
nodes.does: The MOD's supplier-facing sourcing and tendering portal for defence opportunities.

nodes.label: EDIP (EU)
nodes.does: European Defence Industry Programme — the EU's framework for jointly funding and procuring defence capability.

nodes.label: EDIRPA (EU)
nodes.does: EU instrument incentivising common defence procurement among member states.

nodes.label: NSPA framework agreements
nodes.does: NATO Support & Procurement Agency's multinational framework contracts and acquisition support.

nations_procurement.pt: Portugal — public tenders via the national portal (base.gov.pt); defence industry engagement via idD Portugal Defence (iddportugal.pt) and DGRDN.
nations_procurement.ro: Romania — the electronic public procurement system (e-licitatie.ro); defence programmes via the Ministry of National Defence (mapn.ro).
nations_procurement.sk: Slovakia — public tenders via the Electronic Contracting System / ÚVO (uvo.gov.sk); defence acquisition via the Ministry of Defence (mosr.sk).
nations_procurement.hu: Hungary — public procurement via the EKR system (ekr.gov.hu); defence via the Ministry of Defence and Defence Procurement Agency (kormany.hu).
nations_procurement.bg: Bulgaria — the Public Procurement Agency register (app.eop.bg); defence via the Ministry of Defence (mod.bg).
nations_procurement.hr: Croatia — the Electronic Public Procurement Classifieds (eojn.hr); defence via the Ministry of Defence (morh.hr).
nations_procurement.si: Slovenia — public tenders on e-JN (ejn.gov.si); defence via the Ministry of Defence (gov.si/mo).
nations_procurement.al: Albania — the electronic procurement system (app.gov.al); defence via the Ministry of Defence (mod.gov.al).
nations_procurement.mk: North Macedonia — the public procurement bureau (e-nabavki.gov.mk); defence via the Ministry of Defence (mod.gov.mk).
nations_procurement.me: Montenegro — the electronic public procurement system (cejn.gov.me); defence via the Ministry of Defence (gov.me).
nations_procurement.lu: Luxembourg — public tenders via the government portal (pmp.b2g.etat.lu); defence via the Directorate of Defence (defense.gouvernement.lu).
nations_procurement.is: Iceland — public tenders via Ríkiskaup / the central purchasing body (utbodsvefur.is); defence-related procurement via the Coast Guard and Ministry for Foreign Affairs (government.is).
nations_procurement.be: Belgium — federal procurement on e-Procurement (publicprocurement.be); defence buys via DG MR (mil.be).
nations_procurement.tr: Türkiye — defence programmes run through the Presidency of Defence Industries / SSB (ssb.gov.tr); industry engagement via the primes and TEKNOFEST/SAHA events.
nations_procurement.gr: Greece — the national procurement system (promitheus.gov.gr); defence via GDAEED (mod.mil.gr).
nations_procurement.ua: Ukraine — public tenders via Prozorro (prozorro.gov.ua); defence innovation and testing via Brave1 (brave1.gov.ua).
nations_procurement.ca: Canada — federal tenders via CanadaBuys (canadabuys.canada.ca); defence innovation via Defence IDEaS and BOREALIS (canada.ca).
